notes: The API client at / works without signing in: requests, collections and environments are kept in the browser.

Signing in (team workspaces, shared collections, history sync) needs an email server (SMTP, for magic links) or an OAuth app (GitHub, Google or Microsoft). Open /admin to run the onboarding, which collects these settings; the first person to sign in becomes the administrator, so finish the onboarding right after install.

The official all-in-one image runs in sub-path mode (ENABLE_SUBPATH_BASED_ACCESS=true), so one port serves the app at /, the admin dashboard at /admin and the backend at /backend. The desktop app can connect to this instance through the same address.
Database migrations (prisma migrate deploy, as in the official docs) run in the start command before the server starts, so there is no one-shot migration container.

DATA_ENCRYPTION_KEY (32 characters, as the docs require) encrypts the settings stored in the database: keep it with your backups, because the stored settings cannot be read without it. The JWT and session secrets and the token lifetimes are not environment variables in this version: Hoppscotch generates them into the database on first start, and they can be changed in the admin dashboard.
TRUST_PROXY=true makes the backend read the visitor's address from X-Forwarded-For; without it every visitor appears to come from the image's internal proxy and shares one rate-limit bucket.
WHITELISTED_ORIGINS contains this site's HTTPS address plus the desktop app's origins from the official example.
PostgreSQL 17.11 has its own volume and no published port. The data volume keeps the bundle server's signing key, so it survives restarts.
The healthcheck calls /backend/ping on 127.0.0.1 with curl, which the image ships (the image's own healthcheck runs every 2 seconds).
